title: GitOps principles: declarative, versioned and reconciled

videos.script: Somebody changes production by hand during an incident. A week later nobody remembers, and the next deploy quietly undoes it. {{drift}} This course is about a different arrangement. The cluster is described in files, in Git. An agent inside the cluster reads them, and keeps the cluster matching them, all the time. {{loop}} This lesson starts with the idea and its four principles. Declarative, versioned, pulled and continuously reconciled. Each one rules something out. {{principles}} Then you build the lab that every lesson uses, on your own computer. A Kubernetes cluster made by kind, a registry beside it, and a tiny application called bulletin. {{lab}} Last, you write a reconciler yourself, in a dozen lines of shell. You push a commit and watch it arrive. You change the cluster by hand and watch the change disappear. {{reconciler}} And you find the three things a dozen lines cannot do. Those three are why Argo CD and Flux exist, and lessons 3 and 4 are about them. {{limits}}
